claims.claim: Arena serves an embedded React single-page app backed by a REST API and Server-Sent Events (SSE)
The UI lets you hold an interactive chat with a configured agent
The server binds to localhost (127.0.0.1) only
serve accepts a directory containing config.arena.yaml or the config file itself as its argument
promptarena serve --open launches the browser automatically
If config-path is a directory, Arena looks for config.arena.yaml inside it
With no argument serve loads the config from the current directory
promptarena serve with no argument is a valid invocation
promptarena serve ./my-scenario is a valid invocation that loads config from a directory
On startup the server prints its URL and config path
The server runs until Ctrl+C is pressed
The default port is 8080
The UI is served at http://localhost:8080 by default
The port is overridden with -p or --port
promptarena serve --port 3000 is a valid invocation
If the port is in use, serve does not fail and falls back to the next free port
Startup prints the message 'Port 8080 is in use - serving on 8083 instead'
Startup prints the line 'Arena Web UI: http://localhost:8083' for the fallback port
Opening the UI lands on the dashboard
The dashboard reads the loaded config and saved results
On startup Arena hydrates *.json result files from the config's output directory
The dashboard shows providers, scenarios and regions from the loaded config
The dashboard lists completed runs, each opening a detailed results viewer
The dashboard has controls to start a new run and to clear stored results
The dashboard screenshot shows a scenario picker with run cost and duration estimate, a pass-rate dial, tiles for trials, spend, latency and tokens, a provider standings table and a trial matrix
Selecting a trial opens the detailed results viewer for that run
The results viewer shows the transcript with tool calls and their results inline
The results viewer shows per-turn token, cost and latency figures
The results viewer has a scrubber that replays the conversation turn by turn
The run detail view shows message, tool-call, token, cost and latency totals and a replay timeline
The UI subscribes to GET /api/events, an SSE stream of run events
The SSE stream stays open for the life of the page
The SSE stream reconnects automatically if dropped
The status badge in the header switches from Online to Live while a run is in flight
The summary tiles update as each trial lands
Run controls select providers, scenarios and regions to execute
Starting a run issues POST /api/run
The run launches in the background and the request returns immediately
At most 4 runs execute concurrently
Each background run has a 30-minute timeout
Progress streams back over the SSE connection
Each completed run is persisted to the output directory so it survives a restart
Interactive chat lets you pick an agent and provider and supply required template variables
Starting an interactive session issues POST /api/interactive/session
Each message is sent with POST /api/interactive/message
The agent reply renders live over the same SSE stream
Evals can optionally be enabled to score the conversation as it runs
The active agent, provider and connection status sit in a bar above the transcript
Selecting a message opens an inspector on the right
The inspector has Overview, Checks, Raw and Tools tabs
The Raw tab shows the exact message object, including the resolved tool descriptors sent to the provider
The chat screenshot shows a header bar with agent, provider and connection status, the system prompt, a user/assistant exchange, and an inspector showing the raw system message JSON
The server can relay real-time duplex audio for both caller and agent sides to the browser over SSE
Audio is opt-in per client
The frontend requests audio by connecting to GET /api/events?audio=1
promptarena serve --audio-monitor on --audio-rate 24000 is a valid invocation
--audio-monitor accepts auto (default), on or off
--audio-rate accepts 16000, 24000 (default) or 48000
--mock-provider replaces the LLM provider and the self-play role providers with mocks
Mock replacement covers the assistant and the self-play user role; TTS and STT providers are not replaced
--mock-config serves canned scenario responses when used with --mock-provider
promptarena serve --mock-provider --mock-config mock-responses.yaml --open is a valid invocation
In mock mode runs execute end to end with tools still running for real
In mock mode the assistant and self-play turns make no real model calls; TTS and STT providers are not replaced
GET /api/events streams live run events; ?audio=1 enables audio relay
GET /api/config returns the loaded Arena config
GET /api/run-options lists available providers, scenarios and regions
GET /api/results lists completed runs as run_id, scenario_id and provider_id locators
GET /api/results/{id} fetches a single run result
DELETE /api/results clears stored results from memory and disk
GET /api/media/{path...} serves a media artifact such as recorded audio
POST /api/run starts a run in the background
GET /api/interactive/options lists agents and providers for interactive chat
POST /api/interactive/session opens an interactive chat session
POST /api/interactive/message sends a message to a session
GET / serves the embedded React SPA
Pipeline stage events received live show on the run's Trace tab, one row per stage execution with duration and error; only for runs whose events the open page received.
serve exits at startup if the --mock-config file has an unknown key.
